the critical flow rate of a passive portal-systems bypass during 2 hr of portal occlusion in anesthetized dogs is approximately 20% of the preocclusion portal flow rate.
a 2 hr occlusion of the portal vein, either sufficiently or inadequately bypassed, caused no significant liver insults.

a passive portal-system bypass is an effective means of preventing the liver insults caused by acute portal occlusion, and that bypass flow of more than 30% of portal flow is sufficient to maintain the liver in a relatively normal state during portal occlusion.

the portal flow rate of 30% or more of the preocclusion level was necessary to maintain normal splanchnic hemodynamics and metabolism and to protect liver function during 2-h of portal occlusion in the dog model.
a passive portal-system bypass is not necessary to maintain liver function during a 2-hrs interruption of the portal vein flow.

a 2-hour portal occlusion, either sufficiently or not sufficiently bypassed, causes only minimal liver insults.
the liver can withstand a 2-hrs of portal occlusion, but the portal blood flow should be maintained at 30% of the preocclusion levels.
